title: Found Unconscious

rationale.Arterial blood gases: Partially compensated metabolic acidosis. PaO2 normal despite tissue hypoxia (cyanide blocks O2 utilization, not delivery).
rationale.Lactate, serum: Markedly elevated (>10 mmol/L). High lactate with normal carboxyhemoglobin points to cyanide over CO poisoning.
rationale.Carbon monoxide, blood: Carboxyhemoglobin ~10% (mildly elevated, not enough to explain severe acidosis).
rationale.Comprehensive metabolic profile: High anion gap metabolic acidosis. Assess renal function, electrolytes, glucose.
rationale.Electrocardiography, 12 lead: Sinus tachycardia. Evaluate for arrhythmias or ischemic changes from hypoxia.
rationale.100% O2 via non-rebreather: Maximize oxygen delivery. Displace CO from hemoglobin. Supportive for cyanide toxicity.
rationale.Intubation, endotracheal: Airway protection in unconscious patient with high suspicion for cyanide poisoning. Secure before deterioration.
rationale.Intravenous access: Two large-bore IV lines for fluids and medications.
rationale.IV fluids (Normal saline / Lactated Ring: Fluid resuscitation for hypotension and support of hemodynamics in cyanide poisoning.
rationale.Hydroxocobalamin IV (Cyanokit): First-line antidote. Binds cyanide to form cyanocobalamin (renally excreted). Give 5g IV. Repeat if no rapid improvement; third dose with sodium thiosulfate.
rationale.Admit to ICU: Critical care monitoring for cyanide poisoning. Intubated patient needs ventilator management.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents found unconscious with cherry-red skin after being pulled from a burning building with dense acrid smoke. Cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV of ETC) → blocks oxidative phosphorylation → cells cannot use oxygen → tissue hypoxia despite normal PaO2 → anaerobic metabolism → lactic acidosis. Sources: smoke inhalation (burning plastics/wool/synthetics), industrial exposure, sodium nitroprusside infusion. Treatment: hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit — first-line, binds cyanide to form cyanocobalamin which is renally excreted). Alternative: sodium nitrite + sodium thiosulfate (older regimen, risk of methemoglobinemia). Avoid amyl/sodium nitrite if concurrent CO toxicity. Supportive: 100% oxygen, airway management/intubation, IVF, vasopressors if needed. Admit to ICU.
